subject: Re: ACME - SLA/SLO follow-up: latency measurement & remedies
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.co>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: ACME - SLO/SLA follow-up items

Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. A few follow-ups from our side so we can align on the performance commitments before procurement kicks off: 

1) Latency targets: we'd like to understand how you measure latency. Is it server-side first byte, end-to-end request-to-last-byte, or per-token streaming latency? We want to ensure p95/p99 numbers are comparable to our current vendor reports.

2) Throughput & concurrency: our baseline for the evaluation will be a steady-state of ~500 reqs/min (avg request ~1k tokens) and occasional bursts up to 2k reqs/min. We'd like to confirm concurrency limits per-tenant and how connection pooling/streaming affects that.

3) Streaming requirements: many of our product flows use server-sent events and rely on sub-100ms per-token latency for a good UX. Can you confirm if streaming latency is covered under your SLOs or if it requires a separate measurement?

4) Reporting cadence and remedies: what reporting frequency do you provide (daily/weekly/monthly) and what remedies (service credits, rollback/failover) are available if SLOs are missed?

Can you send a draft of the SLA language that covers measurement definitions, exclusions (maintenance, force majeure), reporting cadence, and proposed remedies? Procurement will ask for precise wording.

Attachments: sample_load_profile.csv (we ran a small load test last week)

Thanks —
Jordan
Head of Platform
ACME Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.co>
Cc: Tim O'Neill <tim.oneill@acme.co>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME - SLO/SLA follow-up items

Jordan —

Great to chat — appreciate the clear requirements. Below is a concise recap and the next steps. I attached a draft SLA (acme_sla_draft_v2.pdf) with concrete language; please treat as a starting point.

Recap / proposal:
- Latency measurement: we measure latency as server-side processing time from request receipt to final token emitted (server-side last byte). For streaming flows we also report "time-to-first-byte" (TTFB) and per-token median/p95 over 1-minute windows.
  - SLO suggestion (example): p95 end-to-end server-side latency <= 300ms for non-streaming responses; p95 per-token latency <= 120ms for streaming endpoints (1-minute aggregation).
- Throughput & concurrency: Dedicated pools are sized for sustained throughput. For your baseline (~500 reqs/min, avg 1k tokens) we recommend a 2x headroom reserve. We guarantee capacity for committed concurrency in Dedicated/Reserved plans; burst capacity is handled by autoscaling subject to model warm-up (we expose warm-up windows in capacity APIs).
- Streaming: we treat streaming endpoints as first-class — streaming SLOs are tracked separately (p50/p95 per-token latency over 1-minute windows).
- Measurement windows & exclusions: SLOs are evaluated on rolling windows; scheduled maintenance, upstream network outages (third-party CDN/cloud provider incidents), and customer traffic anomalies (DDoS) are excluded. We record and publish incidents with timestamps for audit.
- Reporting & remedies: weekly latency and error-rate reports via Console + monthly SLA report. Remedies are service credits calculated as a percentage of monthly committed fees for sustained SLO breaches (detailed in draft).

Next steps:
1) I've attached acme_sla_draft_v2.pdf — please review and flag any specific language you want tightened (measurement definitions, exclusion list, credit calculation).
2) If procurement wants, we can convert to DocuSign after legal reviews.
3) I'll loop in our SRE (Marcus) and Head of Product (Rishi) internally for technical clarifications.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: acme_sla_draft_v2.pdf (PDF, 245KB)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Feb 2026 14:47:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: ACME - SLO/SLA follow-up items

Marissa / Rishi —

Quick internal notes after reviewing Marissa's draft and Jordan's asks. Please see inline suggestions for the SLA PDF (I'll send an annotated copy to your inbox). High-level:

1) Measurement definition: prefer to define latency SLOs in terms of server-observed times with explicit mention of clock sync (NTP) and reference to our tracing spans. Add: "Latency is measured at the Redwood ingress service; client-side network time is excluded unless explicitly configured for end-to-end testing."

2) Rolling windows: use 1-minute aggregation for per-token streaming SLOs and 5-minute aggregation for non-streaming p95 to avoid noisy single-request spikes.

3) Exclusions: add explicit language for force majeure, scheduled maintenance (>=72h notice for any maintenance that could affect SLOs), third-party infra incidents (with link to status.redwood.ai incident reports), and customer-configured experimental flags.

4) Remedies: suggest a two-tier credit model: minor breach (single daily window miss) -> 5% of monthly committed fee; sustained breach (monthly availability below agreed threshold) -> 15% credit. Also recommend explicitly excluding credits if the customer is using non-recommended quantization/configs that we label as "experimental" (we'll list these configs in an appendix).

5) Reporting cadence: weekly console reports + monthly signed SLA report. Also include per-incident postmortems for Sev1 incidents within 7 business days.

If this looks good I'll prepare redline text to paste into acme_sla_draft_v3.pdf and send back to Marissa.

- Marcus (SRE)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.co>, Procurement <procurement@acme.co>
Cc: Tim O'Neill <tim.oneill@acme.co>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME - SLA/SLO follow-up items

Jordan / Procurement team —

Thanks for the patience. Per our internal review I've attached acme_sla_draft_v3.pdf which incorporates the following clarifications you asked for:

- Measurement methodology: latency is server-observed at the Redwood ingress (server-side last byte). For streaming endpoints we include time-to-first-byte and per-token p50/p95 over 1-minute aggregation windows. We also explicitly call out clock sync/trace-span correlation steps.
- Aggregation windows: 1-minute for streaming per-token SLOs; 5-minute rolling windows for non-streaming p95/p99 to avoid transient noise.
- Exclusions: scheduled maintenance (we require notification >=72 hours for maintenance that may affect SLOs), third-party provider incidents, customer-driven traffic anomalies and DDoS, and experimental model/quantization configs (listed in appendix).
- Reporting cadence: weekly latency and error breakdowns via Redwood Console; monthly signed SLA report with any sustained breaches and credits applied.
- Remedies/service credits: draft two-tier approach: minor single-window misses = 5% credit; sustained monthly breaches = 15% credit. Exact credit calc is in section 4.2.

Next steps for you: please review the attached and send back any redlines. If procurement is comfortable, we can prepare a DocuSign envelope (link below) once legal reviews the wording. If you need additional telemetry (per-route traces for a 2-week baseline), we can run a short audit — let me know and we'll coordinate scheduling.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.net/ACME/RDW-SLA-v3
Attachment: acme_sla_draft_v3.pdf (PDF, 312KB)

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Email: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0182
